title: UK names 6 banks to lead first digitally native government bond
content: The DIGIT pilot will test distributed ledger technology and onchain settlement for UK sovereign debt, with issuance expected by the first quarter of 2027.

title: Polygon taps TRON’s $94 billion stablecoin supply for seamless cross-border transfers

This innovation aims to simplify cross-border transfers by removing the need for wallet providers, bridges, or fiat ramps. The move enhances interoperability and efficiency within the cryptocurrency ecosystem.

title: Gate bets all-in-one money app is crypto’s biggest consumer trend this year and next

Gate believes this integrated money app will be a major consumer trend in the crypto space.

title: Crypto Long & Short: Zcash and the case for privacy in the age of AI
content: AI has made it cheap to link wallet addresses to the people behind them, and the permanence of the blockchain means records don’t age out. Michael Zhao of Grayscale Research explains how Zcash’s shielded transactions address this problem, and why close to 29% of all ZEC ever mined now sits in the shielded pool.
summary: AI has made it easier and cheaper to link cryptocurrency wallet addresses to individuals, a privacy concern amplified by the blockchain's permanent records. Michael Zhao of Grayscale Research explains how Zcash's shielded transactions offer a solution to this problem, noting that nearly 29% of all ZEC ever mined is now in the shielded pool.

title: Quantum computers threaten exposed private keys rather than blockchains, Europol warns

summary: Europol has warned that quantum computers threaten exposed private keys, rather than blockchains directly, prompting EU law enforcement to urge immediate post-quantum migrations. Developers, exchanges, and users are advised to begin these phased migrations to prevent future unauthorized fund transfers.

title: Cardano gives token issuers power to freeze, seize and restrict assets

title: Everything announced at Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra event
content:
Microsoft just wrapped up a big Windows and Surface-focused keynote in San Francisco.
The biggest announcement was arguably the release details about the Surface Laptop Ultra, its new laptop that’s powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark Arm-based chip. The machine will start at $2,599 for a configuration with an 8-core CPU, 24GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage, and it will be released on October 16th. The laptop also has built-in magnetic USB-C charging instead of the proprietary Surface Connect magnetic charging port. The Verge‘s Tom Warren published a deep dive all about the new laptop. Microsoft also announced that the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a mini PC for developers, is available for preorder for $5,999 ahead of shipping in November.
In addition, Microsoft shared details about some updates coming to Windows, including “Hybrid Intelligence” features that lets Copilot use files on your Windows PC to take actions and a new search experience that lets you do quick actions from the search bar.
You can catch up with all of our coverage from the event right here.

title: ChatGPT for Teens is an ‘unacceptable risk,’ says Common Sense Media
content:
Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that offers reviews of apps, services, and entertainment with a focus on youth safety, today said that OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens is an "unacceptable risk."

title: OpenAI drops another batch of mathematical breakthroughs
content:
OpenAI has revealed solutions to a number of long-standing mathematics problems produced by an unreleased frontier model in a batch of 722 manuscripts, covering 372 result families that group related papers. It extends a run of breakthroughs that have both impressed and unsettled parts of the mathematical community while raising questions about research ethics and academic conduct. According to AGMAI, the newly formed independent advisory group of elite mathematicians put together to work on communicating the results responsibly, the release includes solutions to "hundreds" of open questions.
